questions.question_text: A gym charges a \$40 joining fee, then \$25 for each month of membership, giving $y=25x+40$ where $x$ is the number of months. What does the $25$ represent?

options.text: The cost of each month of membership.

options.why: Reads the rate (gradient) as the starting value; the joining fee is the constant $40$.

options.text: The total cost after one month.
options.why: Confuses the per-month rate with the total $25+40=65$ after one month.
Reads the coefficient as the variable $x$ rather than the cost per month.

questions.solution_text:
The $25$ is the rate, the change for each month.
It is the cost of each month of membership.

questions.question_text: A muffin shop has fixed costs of \$100 each day plus \$2 for every muffin baked. Which equation gives the total daily cost $y$ dollars when $x$ muffins are baked?

options.why: Swaps rate and starting value — treats the \$100 fixed cost as the per-muffin rate.
Subtracts the fixed daily cost instead of adding the fixed starting value.
Adds the two amounts into a single rate, losing the fixed daily cost.

questions.question_text:
The cost of a taxi is $y=4x+10$, where $x$ is the distance in kilometres.
Find the cost of a $25$ km journey.

options.why: Multiplies $4\times25$ but forgets to add the \$10 flag fall.
Adds the flag fall to the distance first, computing $4(25+10)$.

questions.question_text:
The cost of hiring a market stall is $y=8x+20$, where $x$ is the number of hours.
A trader paid \$100.
For how many hours did they hire the stall?

options.why: Divides $100\div8$ without removing the \$20 fixed fee first.
Divides $120\div8$ — adds the fixed fee instead of subtracting it before dividing.
Subtracts $100-20=80$ but forgets to divide by the rate of $8$.

The graph shows the total cost of hiring a party venue: a hire fee plus a charge for each guest.
Use the graph to find the cost for $4$ guests.

options.why: Reads the height of the line at $x=6$ instead of at $x=4$.
Reads the height of the line at $x=2$ instead of at $x=4$.
Reads the $y$-intercept (the hire fee) rather than the value at $x=4$.

questions.question_text:
A phone battery is at $80\%$ charge and drops by $8\%$ each hour, so $y=80-8x$ where $x$ is the time in hours.
Substituting $x=12$ gives $y=-16$.
What does this tell you?

options.text: The model only applies until the battery goes flat; a negative charge is impossible.
The battery sits at $-16\%$ charge after $12$ hours.
options.why: Treats an impossible negative percentage as a real charge level.

options.text: The phone starts recharging once it reaches empty.
options.why: Misreads the negative value as the charge rising rather than the model failing.

options.text: The working must contain an arithmetic error.
options.why: Assumes a mistake rather than recognising the model is outside its valid range.

questions.solution_text:
$y=80-8(12)=-16$
A charge of $-16\%$ cannot happen, so the model only applies until the battery goes flat (at $x=10$).
